targets.text: lobes serves NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B-A3B on the Jetson AGX Orin 64GB
The announcement is only true once a lane actually serves through the gateway on this board -- the 2026-08-25 spike proves the engine, not the deployment.

The stated REASON the Orin declares worker=infeasible is factually wrong for this checkpoint. lobes/machines/orin.py:10-20 and lobes/profiles/builtin/orin.toml:103-128 both assert the NVFP4 lobes 'quantize ACTIVATIONS to FP4 (W4A4 on the MLP path)', naming nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4 explicitly. Its own hf_quant_config.json (fetched 2026-08-25) says otherwise: quant_algo MIXED_PRECISION = W4A16_NVFP4 (group_size 16) on every routed/shared expert up_proj+down_proj, FP8 on mixer in_proj/out_proj, kv_cache_quant_algo FP8. W4A16 is WEIGHT-ONLY -- structurally the same exception the board already runs for senses (int4 W4A16). Both files need the per-checkpoint correction.

The correction is per-CHECKPOINT, not per-board: the W4A4 sentence stays true for the Qwen3.8-27B and Gemma-31B NVFP4 gears and must not be deleted wholesale -- only Lightning is carved out, citing its own hf_quant_config.json.

Adding worker to this board is a THREE-way budget problem the card cannot currently express. builtin/orin.toml:98-101 declares exactly one exclusive_roles group (cortex+senses, MEASURED: 33 GiB + 27.6 GiB against 61.3 GiB with ZERO swap). Lightning's weights measured 17.85 GiB on the Spark (docs/nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b-nvfp4.md:138), so a hosted worker collides with whichever heavy lobe the shape kept -- and lobes init's co-residency guard only refuses what the table declares.

The [[exclusive_roles]] group is only honest if its 'reason' string quotes MEASURED arithmetic from this board, the way the existing cortex/senses group does -- so it cannot be written until a live boot reports associate's real resident footprint.

A stale in-repo doc must be corrected as part of this work. docs/nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b-nvfp4.md:114-125 still records the v0.27.1-on-Thor spike as 'recorded but not yet run' and cites the jetson-ai-lab Orin recipe as a possible reopener; lobes/catalog.py:975-985 says v0.27.1 was in fact tried and also wedged. The doc is behind the catalog on the exact question this idea turns on.
The doc correction lands even if both spikes fail: the stale v0.27.1-on-Thor sentence is wrong today regardless of what the Orin does.

Nothing about the mesh's existing worker seat changes. The Spark GB10 hosts worker today (deviation d1, docs/evidence/2026-08-20-accept-worker-hand-spark.txt) and this box reaches it by proxy -- WORKER_PEER_ORIGIN + WORKER_PEER_PROXY=true are live in ~/.lobes/.env. A local Orin worker is an ADDITION to that topology, and the proxy path stays the fallback if the local lane never validates.
The Spark-hosted worker keeps serving unchanged throughout; nothing in this work edits the Spark's render or its .env.

The gateway, role and proxy machinery is untouched. worker is already a first-class role with a full opt-in mechanism (lobes/profiles/shapes.py OPT_IN_CORE_ROLES, WORKER_FEASIBLE/PEER_ORIGIN/PEER_PROXY/PEER_API_KEY, the thor-worker shape, the 429 pressure policy). Deployment shapes are card-agnostic data -- d1 proved it by rendering thor-worker on the Spark -- so this is a card-profile and image question, not new gateway code.

No gateway BEHAVIOUR is changed: routing, selection, replica-pool and proxy LOGIC are untouched. Only the additive registration that #199 (0.63.0) made generic across role prefixes is extended to a tenth — associate gains its <PREFIX>_* vocabulary in _config.py/_replicas.py/_routing.py/_selection.py exactly as the existing nine have it, and no existing role's behaviour changes. Amended 2026-08-25 by operator decision after #199 merged; the pre-#199 wording forbade wiring that the merge made mandatory.

A TENTH role, 'associate', is now in scope (operator decision, q1): worker minus repo_action -- it executes, drafts, inspects and calls tools, and hands the result back rather than enacting it. Per colleague-stack.md:267-283 every role name becomes a public address across GET /capabilities, a model= alias, a lobes up target, a <PREFIX>_* env vocabulary, six per-role tables, every card profile, every deployment shape and 28 golden .env files.

Every surface colleague-stack.md:267-283 enumerates is actually updated -- GET /capabilities, the model= alias, lobes up, the <PREFIX>_* env vocabulary, six per-role tables, every card profile, every shape, and 28 golden .env files -- or 'associate' is half-served, which #92 forbids.

The image is ALREADY expressible; the SERVE FLAGS are not. Corrects the rejected c3: docker-compose.yml:1326 renders the worker lane as ${WORKER_IMAGE:-${VLLM_NIGHTLY_IMAGE:-vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:8bd082...}}, so a per-role image override is an existing env key -- and the vLLM recipe's vllm/vllm-openai:v0.27.1 is the SAME official Docker Hub repo the fleet already pins, just a release tag instead of a nightly digest. The real gap is that the lane's serve args are one shell-lexed STRING with no extra-args passthrough anywhere in lobes/, and RoleProfile carries only nine knobs plus hf_overrides/allow_long_max_model_len/speculative_config.
WORKER_IMAGE (or its associate-prefixed equivalent) actually reaches the container image at render time, verified by docker compose config, not merely present in env.example.

Eight flags in the published vLLM recipe have NO home in this repo. Expressible today: --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 (RoleProfile.kv_cache_dtype), --max-model-len, --gpu-memory-utilization, the parsers, and the speculative config (WORKER_SPECULATIVE_CONFIG's JSON form is equivalent to the recipe's dotted --speculative_config.* spelling). NOT expressible: --mamba-backend flashinfer, --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float16, --enable-mamba-cache-stochastic-rounding, --mamba-cache-philox-rounds 5, --mamba-cache-mode align, --enable-prefix-caching, --max-num-batched-tokens 16384, --trust-remote-code.

Each of the eight flags is either given a real home that reaches a real flag, or deliberately dropped with a recorded reason -- a knob declared but not wired is exactly the dead declaration #92 exists to prevent.

A GGUF export of Lightning DOES exist, refuting an earlier scope finding. The jetson-ai-lab page fetch reported no GGUF documented; the operator-supplied llama.cpp recipe names ggml-org/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-GGUF:Q4_K_M plus a separate DFlash draft repo. The board already owns the repo's only llama.cpp lane (llamacpp-primary, ENGINE_LLAMA_CPP), but that lane is wired to the PRIMARY_/cortex prefix and pinned to a different image by digest -- serving associate on llama.cpp needs its own lane or a prefix generalisation.
Serving associate on llama.cpp does not silently reuse the PRIMARY_/cortex lane -- the two must be separately addressable, or the board loses its cortex the moment associate starts.

The published utilization makes associate exclusive with every heavy lobe on this board, sharpening c4 from 'may not fit' to 'certainly does not fit alongside either'. The recipe's --gpu-memory-utilization 0.7 is ~42.9 GiB of the board's 61.3 GiB, before the DSpark drafter's own weights and a bfloat16 KV cache that costs roughly double the Spark's fp8_e4m3 pool. Neither cortex (~33 GiB) nor senses (~27.6 GiB) can co-reside with that, so builtin/orin.toml's [[exclusive_roles]] table needs associate added to the group -- and lobes init's co-residency guard only refuses what that table declares.

util 0.7 is the VENDOR's number on an unspecified Orin configuration; the value this repo declares must be the one measured on this board, and if 0.7 is refused at boot the refused value is recorded rather than quietly lowered.

Run the vendor recipes with docker run FIRST, outside lobes entirely. Both recipes are plain docker run invocations with --runtime nvidia (which matches this board's own gpu_access='runtime' csv-mode declaration, builtin/orin.toml:86). Proving the checkpoint serves on sm_87 is an engine question, and answering it inside the scaffold would confound an engine failure with a rendering bug -- the same ordering docs/model-switch-playbook.md already insists on. No .env, profile, shape or catalog change is touched until a lane actually serves.
The docker run probes touch no .env, profile, shape or catalog file; the deployment dir is byte-identical before and after a failed spike.
The lobes fleet operator running the Jetson AGX Orin 64GB, and every Colleague-mesh caller that addresses a generate lane by role name rather than raw model id.
Callers address the lane by role name, never by raw model id -- the 2026-07-31 audit found no consumer doing so, and associate must not become the tenth exception.

The Orin's only local generate lobe above hand is a llama.cpp GGUF cortex measured at 2.61 tok/s -- below its own >=5 tok/s gate, still DECLARED/UNVALIDATED -- and everything faster is a proxy hop to the Spark or Thor. The board declares worker infeasible on a stated reason (W4A4 activations) that is false for this checkpoint.
The 2.61 tok/s baseline and its >=5 tok/s gate are quoted from the board's own spike transcript, not re-derived.

The Orin serves Nemotron 3.5 Lightning locally as 'associate' -- a lobe that does ground work and hands the result back rather than enacting it -- at a measured, published throughput, with the worker seat left free for a future worker/cortex switch.
'Serves locally' means through the gateway's authenticated front (c30/c46), not an open port -- an unauthenticated lane does not satisfy this after_state.

It converts the mesh's slowest box into one that carries its own ground work instead of proxying it, and it corrects a card-profile claim that is provably wrong about a checkpoint the fleet already serves elsewhere.
The W4A4 correction is scoped to Lightning alone and leaves the Qwen3.8-27B and Gemma-31B NVFP4 statements intact.

Both recipes are run verbatim on the physical Orin and each yields a transcript under docs/evidence/ that says GO or NO-GO in its own words: a served /health, a known-answer probe, a structured tool_calls probe, and a single-stream decode figure stated next to the Spark's 75.1 tok/s and this board's 2.61 tok/s -- never next to the vendor's 89 tok/s agentic aggregate.
Every published number names its instrument and its speculation setting, and no figure is compared to the vendor's 89 tok/s agentic aggregate.

The published llama.cpp recipe DOES NOT RUN AS WRITTEN -- MEASURED on this Orin, 2026-08-25. Run verbatim, llama-server exits immediately: 'common_download_get_hf_plan: no GGUF files found in repository ggml-org/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-GGUF' and lists what actually exists -- BF16, Q4_0, Q8_0, and mtp-prefixed variants of each. There is no Q4_K_M in that repo (confirmed independently against the HF API). The recipe's -hfd draft repo apolo13x/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-DFlash-GGUF DOES exist: one file, dflash-NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4.gguf, ~1.1 GB. Minimal correction is Q4_K_M -> Q4_0.

The corrected quantization is chosen on a stated basis, not silently: Q4_0 is the only 4-bit option in the repo, and it is NOT equivalent to the Q4_K_M the vendor claimed to benchmark -- so any throughput or quality number measured here cannot be compared to the vendor's 89 tok/s even setting aside the agentic-aggregate problem.

A corrected recipe is no longer the vendor's recipe, and evidence must say which was run. c18/c21 fund running both VERBATIM; where verbatim fails, the failure is recorded as the primary finding and any corrected re-run is labelled as corrected, with the correction named. Otherwise a passing transcript would silently claim the published configuration works when it does not.
The evidence file states, in its own words, which run was verbatim and which was corrected, and names each correction.

SECURITY: both published recipes stand up an UNAUTHENTICATED 30B endpoint on this box's tailnet. Each binds --host 0.0.0.0 (llama.cpp) or --network host (both), and llama-server's own startup banner warns verbatim: 'CORS is set to allow all origins and no API key is set / this can be a security risk'. PROBED 2026-08-25: this box holds tailnet address 100.81.137.121, so for the whole life of a spike every tailnet peer can reach port 8080 (or 8000) with no credential. The repo's own gateway exists partly to avoid this -- it has an opt-in GATEWAY_API_KEY bearer gate and #127's rule that peer credentials are always a copy of the peer's own inbound key. The frame carried no claim about this before this pass.
Spike endpoints bind loopback (127.0.0.1) or are otherwise unreachable from the tailnet, OR the exposure is time-boxed and explicitly accepted in the transcript -- never left implicit.

MEASUREMENT VALIDITY: the fit arithmetic in this frame rests on numbers that may not mean what they appear to. PROBED 2026-08-25: nvidia-smi reports memory.used [N/A] on this Tegra board, so there is no GPU-memory query -- only tegrastats (RAM 17978/62817MB) and unified-memory 'free'. The board's own profile claims the llama.cpp cortex holds ~33 GiB resident; docker stats reported 27.63 GiB for that same container this session. Any budget claim (c20's util 0.7 ~= 42.9 GiB, c4's exclusive_roles arithmetic) must name which instrument produced it.

Every memory figure recorded in the resulting evidence names its instrument (tegrastats / free / docker stats / the engine's own boot log) -- and the engine's own KV/weights accounting is preferred over any host-side reading.

OPERATIONAL/RECOVERY: this box is mid-spike with its cortex stopped and nothing in the frame owns restoring it. llamacpp-cortex was stopped this session to free 27.6 GiB and the operator has since authorised dropping the remaining lanes as needed. Nothing records what the board's steady state WAS, so a session that ends mid-spike leaves the Orin without a local cortex, embedder or reranker and no note saying they should come back.
The pre-spike container set is captured BEFORE the first stop and restored (or explicitly declared abandoned) at the end, so board state is never left to the transcript reader to reconstruct.

OBSERVABILITY: --rm destroys the evidence, and it already did. The first verbatim llama.cpp run exited on the bad Q4_K_M tag and docker's --rm removed the container before its logs could be captured; only a tail taken by luck mid-run preserved the error. Evidence runs must redirect logs to a file under docs/evidence/ as they happen, not rely on a container surviving long enough to be queried.
Each spike writes its own transcript file as it runs; no finding depends on a container that has already exited.

CONCURRENCY: the vLLM lane's boot is order-sensitive and this spike sequence walks straight into it. docker-compose.yml's own section 5 note records that the nightly's memory profiler ASSERTS free GPU memory stays constant while it profiles, and that concurrent teardown of another container on a shared board trips 'Error in memory profiling' -- prefer one-at-a-time with a settle gap. Stopping the llama.cpp spike and immediately starting the vLLM one at util 0.7 against ~43 GiB of headroom is exactly that hazard.
A memory-profiling failure is reported as a procedure fault and re-run after a settle gap, never recorded as a checkpoint no-go.

llama.cpp lane: NO-GO on this Orin, MEASURED 2026-08-25 (docs/evidence/2026-08-25-spike-lightning-llamacpp-orin.txt). With the quantization corrected to Q4_0 the 17.6 GiB GGUF downloaded in full and then FAILED TO LOAD: 'check_tensor_dims: tensor blk.5.ssm_in.weight not found' -> 'llama_model_load_from_file_impl: failed to load model' -> 'exiting due to model loading error'. blk.5 is a Mamba SSM layer, so the image's llama.cpp cannot find the state-space tensors this GGUF declares. The DFlash draft failed separately and earlier: 'dflash requires ctx_other to be set' -> '[spec] failed to measure draft model memory'. The image is ghcr.io/nvidia-ai-iot/llama_cpp:latest-jetson-orin at llama.cpp version 10373 (38406d597), aarch64 -- NVIDIA's own current Jetson-Orin build.

The failure is attributed correctly: an SSM tensor-name mismatch between this GGUF and llama.cpp b10373 is a BUILD-VERSION gap, not evidence that sm_87 cannot serve the architecture -- a newer llama.cpp has not been tried and would distinguish the two.

The published vLLM recipe ALSO does not run as written -- the THIRD defect, MEASURED 2026-08-25 (docs/evidence/2026-08-25-spike-lightning-vllm-orin.txt). It names the DSpark drafter as nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-DSpark, which does not exist: vLLM's config validation raised 'Repository Not Found' four times, then a pydantic ValidationError for SpeculativeConfig -- 'Invalid repository ID or local directory specified' -- and the API server exited before downloading a single weight. The real repo is nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4-DSpark (verified via the HF model-search API); the recipe simply omits the -NVFP4 infix its own --model argument carries. Minimal correction is that infix.
The corrected DSpark id is the one vLLM actually loaded, verified in the boot log's resolved SpeculativeConfig rather than assumed from the HF search.

sm_87 ADMITS the modelopt_mixed NVFP4 path -- OBSERVED LIVE on this Orin, 2026-08-25, disproving the sm_89+ half of c8. vLLM v0.27.1 accepted quantization=modelopt_mixed and selected a full Marlin fallback stack on Ampere: 'Selected MarlinFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel for ModelOptFp8LinearMethod', 'Using MarlinNvFp4LinearKernel for NVFP4 GEMM', and "Using 'MARLIN' NvFp4 MoE backend out of potential backends: [FLASHINFER_TRTLLM, FLASHINFER_CUTEDSL, FLASHINFER_CUTEDSL_BATCHED, FLASHINFER_CUTLASS, VLLM_CUTLASS, MARLIN, HUMMING, EMULATION]". Attention also resolved natively: 'Using FLASH_ATTN attention backend' / 'FlashAttention version 2'. The engine reached model loading; kernel selection is not yet a working forward pass.

Kernel SELECTION is not kernel CORRECTNESS: vllm-project/vllm#34694 and #49070 report the Marlin NVFP4 fallback producing garbled output and illegal memory accesses on non-Blackwell parts, so a known-answer probe is mandatory before any GO -- a lane that serves fluent nonsense would pass a health check.

vLLM lane: GO on the Jetson AGX Orin 64GB, MEASURED 2026-08-25 (docs/evidence/2026-08-25-spike-lightning-vllm-orin.txt), one correction from the published recipe (the DSpark -NVFP4 infix, c40). Engine vllm/vllm-openai:v0.27.1, quantization=modelopt_mixed on sm_87 via Marlin. Model loading 19.45 GiB; available KV 15.07 GiB; GPU KV cache 1,720,320 tokens; max concurrency at 128,000 tokens/request 13.44x; torch.compile 42.59 s; CUDA graph capture 67 s / 1.71 GiB; init engine 261.28 s. PROBES: known-answer PASS ('Paris', finish=stop); structured tool call PASS (finish_reason=tool_calls, correct name+args, nothing leaked into content) through nemotron_v3 + qwen3_coder. DECODE 900 tokens in 11.15 s and 11.52 s across two runs = ~78-81 tok/s single-stream WITH DSpark speculation.

The ~80 tok/s is measured WITH DSpark speculation at 5 draft tokens and is therefore not comparable to the Spark's 75.1 tok/s no-speculation figure; the honest framings are 'faster than the Spark worker despite far weaker silicon, with speculation doing the work' and '~30x this board's own 2.61 tok/s llama.cpp cortex'.

The util 0.7 budget was measured with EVERY other lane on this board stopped (cortex, senses, embedder, reranker, gateway). It is a solo-boot number and says nothing about co-residency -- c4/c20's exclusive_roles arithmetic still needs its own measurement.

The Orin CLEARS the Mamba2 warmup that wedged the Thor twice -- and c17's explanation was WRONG. The boot log carries the identical line, 'mamba_mixer2.py:596 Warming up Mamba2 SSD Triton kernels...', at 18:58:24 and proceeds normally to KV allocation two minutes later. So --mamba-backend flashinfer did NOT skip the Triton warmup (it governs the SSU backend, logged separately as 'Using flashinfer Mamba SSU backend'); the Orin simply completes a warmup sm_110 hangs on. The Thor no-go is therefore a REAL sm_110/Triton defect, not the missing-flag hypothesis c17 proposed -- which weakens the v4 follow-up's premise.
The claim distinguishes the Triton SSD WARMUP (which the Orin completes) from the FlashInfer SSU BACKEND (which --mamba-backend selects) -- they are separate log lines and separate mechanisms.

DSpark speculation WORKS on sm_87 and is load-bearing for the throughput number. vLLM logged SpecDecoding metrics throughout: mean acceptance length 5.42 / 4.88 / 3.45 / 3.06 across the runs, per-position acceptance decaying 0.76/0.50/0.37/0.24/0.19 at steady state, average draft acceptance 88.3% on short turns settling to ~41.3% on long generation. This resolves park v2 from unmeasured to measured.
Acceptance figures are reported as a decaying range with their per-position rates, not as a single headline number -- steady-state 41.3% is the honest one for long generation.

SECURITY, now REALISED not hypothetical: within seconds of the API server starting, two DISTINCT tailnet peers hit the unauthenticated endpoint -- the transcript records 'INFO: 100.127.105.72:50652 - GET /v1/models HTTP/1.1 200 OK' and 'INFO: 100.105.216.63:55196 - GET /v1/models HTTP/1.1 200 OK', neither of which this session initiated. c30 predicted the exposure; the boot log proves mesh peers actually discovered and queried it. Any adopted lane must sit behind the gateway's GATEWAY_API_KEY rather than binding an open port on the tailnet.
The two tailnet client IPs are quoted from the transcript and were not initiated by this session; the adopted lane binds behind GATEWAY_API_KEY or does not ship.

risks.text: t1 (restore the board) and t8 (measure associate's budget on the board) are in tension: the budget measurement needs the heavy lanes stopped again, so restoring first means a second disruption. Sequence deliberately or accept the double outage.

Marlin NVFP4 correctness on sm_87 is proven only by a single known-answer probe and one tool call. vllm#34694/#49070 report garbled output on this exact fallback; a broader correctness suite before adoption would be prudent and is not yet a task.
The 28 golden .env files and the role test suite were never opened during scope or challenge (scope entry s20). t6's blast radius is asserted, not measured.

MERGE IMPACT (#199, 0.63.0, merged 2026-08-25): the cortex replica pool adds a plural peer family (<PREFIX>_PEER_ORIGINS / _PEER_API_KEYS), GATEWAY_SELF_ORIGIN, a ReplicaCache, live capability fingerprinting and selection — explicitly 'generic across all nine role prefixes'. A TENTH role must therefore also land in lobes/gateway/_config.py, _replicas.py, _routing.py and _selection.py plus their new test suites. This CONTRADICTS confirmed honesty condition h35 on boundary c10 ('No gateway, proxy or role-mechanism source file is modified'), which was confirmed against a pre-#199 tree. Either h35's scope is amended to permit the additive tenth-prefix wiring, or t6 cannot be built as specified.
risks.resolution: RESOLVED by operator decision 2026-08-25: h35 rejected and replaced by h36, which permits the additive tenth-prefix wiring #199 made mandatory while still forbidding any change to gateway BEHAVIOUR. t6 carries two new acceptance criteria pinning that distinction.

risks.text: OPPORTUNITY from #199: the Orin's associate and the Spark's worker serve the SAME checkpoint (Nemotron 3.5 Lightning NVFP4).
